problem:
Find the general solution to the equation

$$
4{x}^{2}{y}^{″}+4x{y}^{′}-y=0,\,x>0.
$$
worked_solution:
Note that the given equation is an instance of the Cauchy-Euler equation. So, we assume that the solutions take the form $y={x}^{\lambda }.$ Differentiating $y$ with respect to $x$ gives

$$
{y}^{′}=\lambda {x}^{\lambda -1},\,{y}^{″}=\lambda (\lambda -1){x}^{\lambda -2}.
$$

Substituting the above to our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}4{x}^{2}\cdot \lambda (\lambda -1){x}^{\lambda -2}+4x\cdot \lambda {x}^{\lambda -1}-{x}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ 4\lambda (\lambda -1){x}^{\lambda }+4\lambda {x}^{\lambda }-{x}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ {x}^{\lambda }[4\lambda (\lambda -1)+4\lambda -1] & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the auxiliary equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}4\lambda (\lambda -1)+4\lambda -1 & =0 \\ 4{\lambda }^{2}-1 & =0 \\ (2\lambda +1)(2\lambda -1) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the roots are $\lambda =\pm \frac{1}{2}.$
Therefore, the general solution is

$$
y(x)={c}_{1}{x}^{1/2}+{c}_{2}{x}^{-1/2}.
$$
